localChanges: Every layer was a canvas the size of the whole world — 2560x1920 at 80x60 scale 2, and seven of them, 137.4 MB before a tile is drawn, growing with the map. A layer is now the size of the portal that composites it, with `#originX` and `#originY` saying which world pixel sits at its top left corner: 40.0 MB for the same world, and a world twice the size costs the same again.

That means a tile no longer has one fixed place on a canvas, and because the world wraps it can have several places or none. Layers are handed the places to draw in rather than working them out from the tile's co-ordinates — `drawTile(tile, offsetX, offsetY)`, called once per place — so `Portal` has no wrap offsets to composite any more, and the overflow `CityNames` used to draw a canvas-width away to survive being tiled is now just another placement. Moving the view blits the overlap across and draws only the strips it uncovers.

Layers record what they changed, and `Portal.render()` composites those regions rather than the whole canvas, which is what restricting the blink tick to the active unit's region needed: `ActiveUnit` is the topmost layer, so un-drawing it means restoring the pixels beneath it. A blink composite is 0.006 megapixels and 5.5 `drawImage` calls against 10.5 and 7 for a full one. Regions are unioned until none overlap, because compositing a pixel twice doubles up anything drawn with alpha, and past half the canvas or eight regions it composites the lot instead. What a tile draws past its own square is recorded as it is drawn rather than declared per layer, so the city glyph, a yield icon and the copy behind a stack all reach the composite without the sprite sizes being second-guessed.

Verified in the browser on an 80x60 world at scale 2 in a 1712x873 portal: after panning, city windows, overlay toggles and blinks the incrementally composited portal is pixel-identical to a full composite, and a viewport reached by short scrolling hops is pixel-identical to the same viewport drawn from nothing — 0 of 1,494,576 pixels differ in each case. The geometry underneath is exhaustively tested offline.

Fixed on the way: the resize handler assigned `mapPortal.width` and `height` unconditionally, and assigning either clears a canvas even when the value has not changed. A resize that resized nothing therefore wiped the map, and with the portal compositing only what changed it put nothing back.
